description: CESAR-P calculates building energy demand for districts using a bottom-up EnergyPlus workflow. Empa publishes the Python code to prepare building parameters, generate IDF inputs, run simulations and process results, with parallel execution supported. Users supply building footprints and heights, construction years, use types and hourly EPW weather; shading requires neighbouring geometry. Default outputs summarise annual heating, cooling and domestic-hot-water demand, with hourly series available on request. Geographic coverage follows the supplied district, and the README describes Swiss scaling applications. GitHub distributes the source under AGPL-3.0, allowing free reuse. The documented dependency range is EnergyPlus 8.5 to 9.5, and some inputs use spreadsheets. A limitation is that clustering and upscaling are outside CESAR-P itself. These version and scope limits matter for reproducing a city-scale study. The model can compare retrofit measures and their energy, cost and emission consequences. Related record model-energyplus supplies the underlying simulator. No building data were downloaded and no simulation was run.
